transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-06
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (BluePeak Head of ML), Samir Patel (BluePeak Infra), Jules Carter (BluePeak PM)

Auto-summary: Quick sync on throughput tuning. Major topics: continuous batching config, concurrency targets, observed queueing, tail latency spikes, plan for 24h steady-state run and next benchmarking steps.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for jumping on — can you all hear me ok?
[00:04] Marta Ruiz: yep loud and clear, thanks Alex.
[00:07] Jules Carter: hi — sorry running a bit late, joining now.
[00:10] Priya Rao: no worries. quick agenda: recap last week's change (batching window to 40ms), current throughput/latency numbers, queueing behavior, and next steps — we'll propose config tweaks.
[00:20] Samir Patel: quick context from infra: we spun up the 4-node test cluster on gcp-n1 with a mix of A100-ish hardware, we're seeing consistent token/s numbers but there's this intermittent queueing we wanted to show.
[00:30] Priya Rao: cool — ok so last week when we increased the batching window to 40 ms we saw average throughput bump from ~1.2k tokens/sec to 1.9k tokens/sec for the demo workload, but p95 latency went from 180ms to about 260ms, and we saw occasional p99 spikes to 900-1,100ms.
[00:51] Marta Ruiz: that's the problem area — product is sensitive to p99 latency spikes, our SLA target is p95 < 300ms and p99 < 700ms.
[01:02] Alex Chen: got it. can you remind us about the request pattern — bursty vs steady?
[01:06] Jules Carter: mostly bursty — lots of short chat-like requests, median tokens per request ~55, but we do have long tails (200+ tokens) for a subset of calls.
[01:18] Priya Rao: right — the long tails are causing KV cache pressure and occasionals cause batching delays because long requests occupy the GPU longer.
[01:27] Samir Patel: also we have a concurrency cap at the infra layer of 16 containers per node; with the current autoscaling settings we hit the scheduling queue occasionally which contributes to the spikes.
[01:38] Alex Chen: ok thanks. Priya, do you have the perf graphs?
[01:40] Priya Rao: yes — I shared the perf deck link in the chat (link: https://redwood.ai/perf/bluepeak/2026-05-06). pulling up the latest traces — you can see continuous-batching batches per second increased and GPU utilization went from 62% to about 85%.
[01:57] Marta Ruiz: high utilization is good for cost, but we can't sacrifice the p99 beyond 700ms.
[02:03] Priya Rao: agreed. a few things to propose: 1) hybrid batching: keep prefix/kv caching aggressive for short requests, but cap batch size for requests that are likely to be long; 2) introduce a concurrency soft-limit per model worker so long requests don't starve short ones; 3) small queueing tier: set a 100ms micro-queue to coalesce very short bursts but fall back quickly.
[02:28] Jules Carter: can you explain hybrid batching more — what's the heuristic?
[02:31] Priya Rao: simple heuristic: if request estimated tokens < 80 we allow to join continuous batch up to size 48 or 60 (configurable); if estimated tokens > 80 we route to a separate lane with smaller batch cap 8-12 to keep latency for short ones low. estimate is model-informed (prompt length + user history).
[02:48] Samir Patel: curious about how estimates affect correctness — we have dynamic prompts and it's hard to predict sometimes.
[02:53] Priya Rao: totally — estimate is probabilistic. we add a short pre-pass token-length check which is cheap. it's not perfect, but in practice it reduces long-request contamination of short-request batches.
[03:05] Alex Chen: good. what about queueing and concurrency?
[03:08] Priya Rao: for concurrency we recommend two knobs: worker_concurrency (how many requests a single worker handles concurrently) and request_token_timeout (max time to hold a request in batch queue). setting worker_concurrency to 6 for this model gave us a good balance in earlier tests.
[03:22] Marta Ruiz: previous run had concurrency at 8, we saw throughput high but occasional p99 spikes. would 6 be safer?
[03:28] Priya Rao: yes — our internal runs show p95 remains similar while p99 drops significantly when we throttle concurrency a bit.
[03:34] Jules Carter: what about autoscale? we hit scheduling lag — do we need different cluster sizing?
[03:39] Samir Patel: right now cluster scales by pod CPU, but model containers saturate GPU and we don't trigger fast enough. we could switch to GPU-aware metrics or add headroom nodes.
[03:49] Alex Chen: adding headroom sounds sensible — like reserve 15% spare capacity and bump the burst pool. that reduces scheduling queuing. cost tradeoff minimal vs SLA risk.
[03:59] Marta Ruiz: acceptable if we can show the numbers. what's the projected cost increase?
[04:03] Alex Chen: I'll put numbers in the follow-up — we have a small calc for extra reserved nodes vs p99 reduction.
[04:10] Priya Rao: couple more observations: KV cache hit rate dropped during the long-request bursts — because long sequences flush cache regions. Suggest bumping cache size for this model and enable prefix pinning for common prefixes. That improved effective throughput in our sim by ~8%.
[04:27] Samir Patel: are there memory implications if we increase KV cache? we have node memory limits.
[04:31] Priya Rao: small increase — within the A100 memory headroom we provisioned in the cluster test; we can give a config that is conservative.
[04:38] Jules Carter: regarding the 24h run — what exactly do you need from us?
[04:41] Priya Rao: we need a steady-state run with the hybrid batching + concurrency=6 + small micro-queue enabled. Please run for 24 hours with your production-ish traffic (or replay logs) so we can observe tail behavior. Collect traces and upload logs to the shared S3 bucket.
[04:58] Samir Patel: we can do that — I'll provision the test cluster and run replay. we'll start Friday after our change window.
[05:04] Marta Ruiz: are we concerned about function calling or tooling affecting latencies? we use a few external tools that sometimes block.
[05:12] Priya Rao: good point — we recommend isolating tool calls to async paths where possible, and for sync flows make sure those calls are outside the critical model path or use timeouts. We'll include notes in the config doc.
[05:24] Alex Chen: any blockers on security/compliance for running 24h replay?
[05:27] Samir Patel: none — logs are internal. we'll mask PII in the replay per the plan.
[05:31] Jules Carter: ok. can you restate the immediate changes we'll try?
[05:34] Priya Rao: sure — 1) hybrid batching heuristic (short vs long lane), 2) worker_concurrency -> 6, 3) micro-queue 100ms for short bursts, 4) increase KV cache size + prefix pinning for common prompts, 5) reserve 15% headroom nodes to reduce scheduling queueing.
[05:53] Marta Ruiz: sounds good. curious on the expected delta — do you have an estimate for p99 improvement?
[05:58] Priya Rao: early sims show p99 dropping from ~1,000ms to ~450-600ms depending on burstiness. p95 should remain under 300ms. Throughput might slightly drop from 1.9k tokens/s to ~1.7k tokens/s in worst-case, but cost per useful token improves because we reduce tail re-tries.
[06:17] Alex Chen: excellent. next steps recap: Priya share config + perf graphs by 05-08, Samir to provision and run 24h by 05-10, Alex to send pricing for dedicated nodes and headroom calc by 05-07.
[06:30] Jules Carter: for the dedicated nodes question — is there a minimum commit?
[06:33] Alex Chen: yes typical dedicated commits start at 3 months minimum and scale; I'll include options.
[06:38] Marta Ruiz: any thought about using Redwood Dedicated vs hosted with these tweaks?
[06:42] Priya Rao: Dedicated gives more control for concurrency and guaranteed capacity which makes these tuning knobs more predictable. Hosted can work but you'd rely on more aggressive fallbacks and routing policies. We'll lay out pros/cons in the follow-up.
[06:55] Samir Patel: during the 24h run we'll also capture GPU counters; does Redwood need any special agent?
[06:59] Priya Rao: no special agent, we just need the perf traces and the system metrics (nvidia-smi, dstat) and Redwood's trace ID annotations. We'll share a listing of exact logs to upload.
[07:10] Alex Chen: ok last thing — any blockers from BluePeak side?
[07:13] Marta Ruiz: just internal scheduling for the test window; otherwise good.
[07:17] Jules Carter: fine here.
[07:19] Alex Chen: great — thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the deck and config.
[07:23] Meeting end.

Notes about transcription: occasional speaker overlap, some model names got auto-corrected in the transcript (A100 referenced as A-naught), small punctuation artifacts.
